drafts.headline: Cost of sales forecasts run about 1.6 times too low for EGCH.
drafts.plain: The method misses this driver in the same direction almost every time, not at random. That is a fixable defect rather than noise — find what is wired wrong before adding any correction factor.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.496 log (about 1.6 times too low), average miss 0.618, wrong in the same direction in 78% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=55).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run of the same name where the sign no longer holds across bootstrap blocks.
drafts.declined: The same defect counted again: this line's bias is a consequence of the plant replacement registered from DRAFT-EGCH-05 (every level driver projects the pre-FY2020 plant into the years the new complex reported), and one cause is recorded once.

drafts.headline: While a project is under construction, its interest and currency losses go to the asset, not the income statement.
drafts.plain: Under IAS 23 and its Egyptian equivalent, the interest on a loan that funds a qualifying asset — and the exchange loss on that loan — is capitalised into the asset until it is ready for use. So a borrowing rate formed from the income-statement charge during construction understates what the loan actually costs, and a currency driver that charges the revaluation to profit invents a loss the company will never book there. Form the rate on the loan's own terms, put the construction-period charge on the balance sheet, and move it to the income statement only when the asset is commissioned.
drafts.evidence: Bias -1.276 log (about 3.6 times too low), average miss 1.372, wrong in the same direction in 86% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=28).
drafts.why_scope: The mechanism is an accounting standard, not a company quirk — any issuer with a qualifying asset under construction shows it. It extends L-041/L-044: the rate can be formed on exactly the borrowings that bear it and still be wrong while the charge is capitalised.
drafts.overturned_by: An issuer that expenses all borrowing costs as incurred, where the rate formed on the income-statement charge matches the loan's disclosed cost and the currency revaluation appears in profit in the year of the devaluation.

drafts.headline: EGCH: every level driver projects a plant that no longer exists.
drafts.plain: The 1960 electrolytic plant was shut inside the window and replaced by a gas-fed urea complex with about twelve times its revenue, with two loss years on either side. A rule that holds any level flat, or grows it on its own trend, from an origin before FY2020 is forecasting the old plant into years the new one reported, so revenue, cost and profit all come out far too low with a sign that never changes. On this name the record before and after the replacement must be read as two records.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.596 log (about 1.8 times too low), average miss 0.812, wrong in the same direction in 67% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=55).
drafts.why_scope: One company replaced its entire asset base inside the window; that is this name's history, not its class's. L-043 already carries the general form (a projected asset base cannot see an acquisition).
drafts.overturned_by: A re-run of the same rules on origins FY2020 onward only, where the revenue bias no longer holds its sign across bootstrap blocks.

drafts.headline: The net forecast loses to assuming no change.
drafts.plain: At 4 of 5 horizons, simply carrying last year's number forward beat the model. A method that cannot beat 'no change' has not earned the precision it displays, and should be published as a range or not at all.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 1, 2, 3, 5, worst -1.099.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run where the model beats the freeze benchmark at a majority of horizons.
drafts.declined: A second observation of L-049 (AMOC): the method loses to 'no change' on the profit line, here net skill vs freeze -0.559 over 23 scoreable cells. Recorded as evidence for the existing lesson and in the training record and the study's section 7, not as a new lesson; the EGX checkpoint review is where a finding that now holds on two names is widened.

drafts.headline: The cost of sales error is the company, not the currency.
drafts.plain: Re-running every forecast with perfect foresight of inflation barely improves it. So devaluation is not the explanation, and looking for a macro fix would waste the effort.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 0.618 as known, 0.580 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only 6.1%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same decomposition puts most of the error on the macro path.
drafts.declined: Cost of sales is a consequence of the plant replacement registered from DRAFT-EGCH-05; that it is a company error rather than a macro one is already what that lesson says.

drafts.headline: A statutory-rate tax driver must first check whether the company pays current tax at the origin.
drafts.plain: Tax by formula at the statutory rate is the right rule for a regime, but a company carrying forward large losses, or taking an accelerated first-year deduction on new plant, books no current tax for years and then a deferred charge or credit that the formula cannot see. Read the current-tax line and the deferred-tax note at the origin before applying the rate; where current tax is nil, say so and carry the zero-tax case beside the statutory one rather than assuming it away.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 1.500 as known, 2.028 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only -35.2%.
drafts.why_scope: This is a method rule about which disclosure a tax driver reads, not a fact about fertiliser or about EGCH; the same formula would miss on any loss-carrying issuer.
drafts.overturned_by: A run on a company whose current tax at every origin equals the statutory rate on profit before tax, where the formula's error is inside the other drivers' noise.

drafts.headline: The credit interest bias changes direction between regimes.
drafts.plain: It runs one way in one period and the other way in the next. Averaging them produces a correction that is wrong in both. Record it, do not correct for it.
drafts.evidence: By era: E1 old plant, pre-float +1.133; E2 old plant post-float / transition +0.924; E3 KIMA-2 operating, devaluations -3.950.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: A longer record in which one sign dominates across all regimes.
drafts.declined: An instance of L-047 (TMGH): in a market with three currency regimes inside the window a bias that changes sign between eras is the normal case. Reported in the training record's by-era table as instability, never corrected for; EGCH is the second name showing it and that is recorded here rather than as a new id.

drafts.headline: A correction to selling worked and must still be checked against the rest of the book.
drafts.plain: A fudge factor that improves this one name can be hiding a defect in how we set the model up. Before adopting it, check it matches how that driver is built everywhere else.
drafts.evidence: Applied -0.019 at origin FY2015; average miss changed -0.019.
drafts.why_scope: If the correction turns out to be fixing our own mis-specification, the lesson is ALL and is about specification. If the company is genuinely unusual, it is STOCK.
drafts.overturned_by: Evidence that the driver is built the same way across the book and this name still needs the correction.
drafts.declined: Not a finding: the half-strength correction improved the adjusted-vs-raw score by +0.01 to +0.04 at one origin and the same correction hurt at the other origins tested (selling 1 helped / 2 hurt, admin 2 / 1). It stays a watch flag in corrections_log.json, graded live and acted on by nobody, which is what the two-clause test says; a lesson would give one origin's noise a number.
